texts.facts: This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to quash Ext.P6 stop memo issued by the Secretary of the Malur Grama Panchayat, i.e., the 1st respondent dated 28.05.2018, stating that waste is being discharged from the establishment run by the petitioner causing serious prejudice to the residents of the locality, failing which, appropriate coercive action will be taken by the Panchayat to stop the unit run by the petitioner. Brief material facts for the disposal of the writ petition are as follows: 2. Petitioner is operating a rice flour manufacturing unit under the name "Malabar Food Products", which, according to the petitioner, is being carried on by securing necessary clearances from all statutory authorities. It is submitted that, license was being issued by the Panchayat following Ext.P1 licence issued in the year 2006, by paying the licence fee, evident from the receipt produced as Ext.P1(3) dated 22.03.2018. Ext.P2 is the consent to operate issued by the Pollution Control Board valid up to 31.01.2023, and Ext.P3 is the licence issued by the authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Therefore, according to the petitioner, the unit is being carried on with necessary licences. 3. However, due to personal animosity between the neighbour, i.e., the 3rd respondent and the petitioner, 3rd respondent started to create one or other hindrances to the petitioner. He has earlier filed a writ petition before this Court, demanding action by the 1 st respondent to close down the unit, in which, 1st respondent has filed Ext.P4 counter affidavit, stating that, petitioner has not caused any nuisance. Later, the writ petition was disposed of, as per Ext.P5, directing the 1 st respondent to visit the site after giving due notice and verify if the petitioner is running the unit with statutory compliances and if any violation is observed, to issue notice to the petitioner and abate the same. Erayi Krishnan vs Malur Grama Panchayat on 13 December, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22885362/ 2 4. It is the case of the petitioner that, without proper application of mind and merely believing the complaints filed by 3rd respondent and others, 1st respondent has issued Ext.P6 stop memo. Learned counsel also submitted that, during the pendency of this writ petition, a varied consent viz., Ext.P7 was also secured from the Pollution Control Board with respect to the management of waste water flown from the unit. That apart, it is submitted that, a fresh licence application is submitted before the Secretary of the 1st respondent, seeking issuance of D&O licence, taking into account the varied consent issued by the Pollution Control Board. However, no action is taken in the application and therefore, petitioner is entitled to continue the operations, deeming that the licence is issued by the Secretary. 5. A report is submitted by the Environmental Engineer of the Pollution Control Board and has produced the consent given to the petitioner. Ext.R2(b) communication dated 19.06.2018 is issued by the Board, informing that, petitioner is carrying on washing of rice in the unit and there are no mechanism provided to manage the water arising out of the cleaning process. Other aspects with respect to the manner in which the unit is run by the petitioner is also pointed out. 6. The 3rd respondent has filed a detailed counter affidavit, explaining the difficulties faced by the residents of the locality, consequent to the waste accumulated in the premises of the unit run by the petitioner, which is causing serious pollution and other problems to the residents of the locality. Apart from the same, the report submitted by the Pollution Control Board is seriously objected, stating that the inspection said to have been conducted on 13.06.2018 was without notice to the 1st respondent Panchayat or to the neighbouring residents of the locality, including the 3rd respondent. That apart, it is pointed out that, the variation of consent was granted without any information to the Panchayat as well as the people residing in the locality, and further that, due to the sound emanated from the machineries of the unit, there is clear air and sound pollution, which has not been taken note of by the Pollution Control Board while granting the consent.
